_about: Plain-English definitions for every money figure on School Money. label: short heading; plain: one sentence a parent can read; how: how the number is worked out; source: where it comes from (CFR = council-run schools' Consistent Financial Reporting return, AAR = academies' Accounts Return); ifs: optional key path into pipeline/money/data/ifs_context.json for wider context.

total_income.label: Total income
total_income.plain: All the money the school received in the year, mostly government funding plus anything it raised itself.
total_income.how: Government grants plus self-generated income (lettings, catering, donations and the like) for the school's financial year. Early CFR years are adjusted so that money moved into capital projects (E30) is not counted twice.
total_income.source: CFR total income (I01 to I18 less E30) / AAR Total Income

grant_funding.label: Grant funding
grant_funding.plain: Money that arrives as grants, nearly all of it from the government through the council or the Department for Education.
grant_funding.how: The sum of the grant lines in the school's return. For academies this can include a small amount of non-government grants; see 'Government grants' for the government-only figure.
grant_funding.source: CFR lines I01 to I07, I15, I16 and I18 / AAR Total Grant Funding

grant_funding_government.label: Government grants
grant_funding_government.plain: Grant money from the government only, with charitable and other grants and payments from other academies taken out.
grant_funding_government.how: For council-run schools this is the same as grant funding. For academies it is total grant funding less non-government grants and income received from other academies.
grant_funding_government.source: CFR grant funding / AAR Total Grant Funding less Non-Government and Academies lines

sen_funding.label: Special needs funding
sen_funding.plain: Extra money the school gets to support pupils with special educational needs.
sen_funding.how: Top-up and other SEN funding received from the council's high-needs budget, as reported by the school.
sen_funding.source: CFR line I03 SEN funding / AAR SEN funding

pupil_premium.label: Pupil premium
pupil_premium.plain: Extra funding for pupils from lower-income families, children in care and service families.
pupil_premium.how: The pupil premium grant received in the year. Academies do not break this out in their accounts return, so it only shows for council-run schools.
pupil_premium.source: CFR line I05 Pupil premium / AAR pupil premium is not broken out

self_generated_income.label: Money the school raised itself
self_generated_income.plain: Income the school earned or was given rather than granted, such as lettings, catering, trips and donations.
self_generated_income.how: The sum of the self-generated income lines: facilities and services, catering, insurance receipts, contributions to visits, donations and community facilities.
self_generated_income.source: CFR lines I08 to I13 and I17 / AAR Total Self Generated Funding

donations.label: Donations
donations.plain: Gifts of money to the school from parents, the PTA, charities and local businesses.
donations.how: Donations and private funds reported as revenue income, plus (for council-run schools) voluntary income given for buildings and equipment.
donations.source: CFR lines I13 and CI03 / AAR Donations and/or voluntary funds

donations_revenue.label: Donations (day-to-day)
donations_revenue.plain: Gifts of money the school can spend on day-to-day running, such as PTA contributions.
donations_revenue.how: Donations and private funds reported in the school's revenue income for the year. It can include money passed on by a parents' association, so it can overlap with PTA income and the two are never added together.
donations_revenue.source: CFR line I13 Donations and/or private funds / AAR Donations and/or voluntary funds

donations_capital.label: Donations (buildings and equipment)
donations_capital.plain: Gifts given specifically for buildings, grounds or equipment rather than day-to-day costs.
donations_capital.how: Voluntary or private capital income reported by council-run schools. Academies report capital donations differently, so this is CFR only.
donations_capital.source: CFR line CI03 Voluntary or private income / not in the AAR

lettings_income.label: Lettings
lettings_income.plain: Money from hiring out the hall, pitches, rooms or car park outside school hours.
lettings_income.how: Income from rentals and lettings as reported by the school.
lettings_income.source: CFR line I08a Income from lettings / AAR Income from rentals and lettings

facilities_income.label: Facilities and services
facilities_income.plain: Money from things the school provides for a fee, such as lettings, breakfast clubs, music tuition or uniform sales.
facilities_income.how: All income from facilities and services, which includes lettings.
facilities_income.source: CFR line I08 Income from facilities and services / AAR Income from facilities and services

catering_income.label: Catering income
catering_income.plain: Money paid for school meals and other food the school sells.
catering_income.how: Income from catering as reported by the school. Compare it with catering costs to see whether meals break even.
catering_income.source: CFR line I09 Income from catering / AAR Income from catering

teacher_pension_ni_grants.label: Pension and National Insurance grants
teacher_pension_ni_grants.plain: Grants that cover rises in what the school must pay towards teachers' pensions and staff National Insurance.
teacher_pension_ni_grants.how: Government grants that pass straight through to pay and pension costs, so they add to income and spending by the same amount without adding spending power. No return separates them out, so the site shows the line that contains them (Other DfE grants) rather than a figure for these grants alone.
teacher_pension_ni_grants.source: Not separated in the CFR or AAR: inside CFR line I18 (I06 from 2025-26) and AAR Other DfE revenue grants

non_government_grants.label: Non-government grants
non_government_grants.plain: Grants from charities, trusts and businesses rather than the government.
non_government_grants.how: Non-government grant income as reported by academies. Council-run schools include it within other grants.
non_government_grants.source: AAR Non-Government grants / not separated in the CFR

total_expenditure.label: Total spending
total_expenditure.plain: Everything the school spent in the year on staff, buildings, energy, learning resources and services.
total_expenditure.how: The sum of all revenue expenditure lines in the school's return for the year.
total_expenditure.source: CFR total expenditure (E01 to E29, E31 and E32) / AAR Total Expenditure

teaching_staff.label: Teachers
teaching_staff.plain: Pay, pension and National Insurance for the school's teachers.
teaching_staff.how: Teaching staff costs including on-costs, as reported by the school.
teaching_staff.source: CFR line E01 Teaching staff / AAR Teaching staff

supply_staff.label: Supply teachers
supply_staff.plain: What the school paid for cover when teachers were absent or posts were empty.
supply_staff.how: Supply teaching staff plus agency supply teachers, as the DfE's benchmarking tool (FBIT) counts them. Supply teacher insurance is not included, so the figure compares like with like across years and sectors.
supply_staff.source: CFR lines E02 and E26 / AAR Supply teaching staff and Agency supply teaching staff

education_support_staff.label: Support staff
education_support_staff.plain: Pay for teaching assistants, learning mentors, librarians and other staff who support learning directly.
education_support_staff.how: Education support staff costs including on-costs.
education_support_staff.source: CFR line E03 Education support staff / AAR Education support staff

admin_clerical_staff.label: Office staff
admin_clerical_staff.plain: Pay for the school office, finance and administrative staff.
admin_clerical_staff.how: Administrative and clerical staff costs including on-costs.
admin_clerical_staff.source: CFR line E05 Administrative and clerical staff / AAR Administrative and clerical staff

premises_staff.label: Site staff
premises_staff.plain: Pay for caretakers, cleaners and other staff who look after the buildings.
premises_staff.source: CFR line E04 Premises staff / AAR Premises staff

catering_staff.label: Catering staff
catering_staff.plain: Pay for kitchen and dining staff employed by the school.
catering_staff.how: Catering staff costs including on-costs. Schools that buy in catering show those costs under bought-in services instead.
catering_staff.source: CFR line E06 Catering staff / AAR Catering staff

other_staff_costs.label: Other staff costs
other_staff_costs.plain: Other people costs such as training, recruitment, staff insurance and other staff not listed above.
other_staff_costs.how: Other staff, indirect employee expenses, staff development and staff-related insurance lines added together.
other_staff_costs.source: CFR lines E07 to E11 / AAR other staff cost lines

total_staff.label: All staff costs
total_staff.plain: Everything the school spent on people, which is usually about four pounds in every five.
total_staff.how: The sum of every staff cost line, including supply and agency staff.
total_staff.source: CFR Staff total (E01 to E03, E05, E07 to E11 and E26) / AAR Total Staff Costs

premises.label: Buildings and grounds
premises.plain: Keeping the buildings and grounds maintained, cleaned and safe.
premises.how: Building maintenance and improvement, grounds maintenance, cleaning and caretaking added together.
premises.source: CFR lines E12 to E14 / AAR premises lines

energy.label: Energy
energy.plain: Gas, electricity and other fuel for heating, lighting and running the school.
energy.how: Energy costs as reported by the school.
energy.source: CFR line E16 Energy / AAR Energy

occupation.label: Rates, water and other building costs
occupation.plain: Business rates, water, insurance and other costs of occupying the buildings.
occupation.how: Water and sewerage, rates and other occupation costs added together.
occupation.source: CFR lines E15, E17 and E18 / AAR occupation lines

catering.label: Catering supplies
catering.plain: Food and other supplies for school meals, and bought-in catering contracts.
catering.how: Catering supplies as reported by the school.
catering.source: CFR line E25 Catering supplies / AAR Catering supplies

educational_supplies.label: Learning resources
educational_supplies.plain: Books, equipment, software and computers used for teaching, plus exam fees.
educational_supplies.how: Learning resources (not ICT), ICT learning resources and examination fees added together. Administration software (CFR line E20D, split out from 2024-25) is left out in every year, as FBIT does, so years compare like with like.
educational_supplies.source: CFR lines E19 to E21 less E20D / AAR learning resources and exam fees

supplies_services.label: Supplies and services
supplies_services.plain: Everyday running costs such as office supplies, insurance and special facilities.
supplies_services.how: Administrative supplies, other insurance premiums and special facilities added together.
supplies_services.source: CFR lines E22 to E24 / AAR supplies and services lines

bought_in_services.label: Bought-in services
bought_in_services.plain: Professional services the school pays other organisations for, such as HR, legal, IT support or therapy.
bought_in_services.how: Bought-in professional services for the curriculum and for other purposes added together.
bought_in_services.source: CFR lines E27 and E28 / AAR Bought in professional services

revenue_reserve.label: Reserve
revenue_reserve.plain: The school's savings: money carried over from previous years that it can still spend.
revenue_reserve.how: The revenue balance at the end of the year, committed and uncommitted together. Below zero means the school owes money to the council or trust.
revenue_reserve.source: CFR lines B01 and B02 / AAR Revenue reserve

revenue_reserve_incl_trust_share.label: Reserve including trust share
revenue_reserve_incl_trust_share.plain: The academy's own reserve plus its share of money held centrally by its trust.
revenue_reserve_incl_trust_share.how: Only academies report this. The trust's central reserve is shared out among its schools in proportion to pupils.
revenue_reserve_incl_trust_share.source: AAR Revenue reserve including trust share / not in the CFR

reserve_committed.label: Committed reserve
reserve_committed.plain: Savings the school has already earmarked for something, such as a building project.
reserve_committed.how: The committed revenue balance reported at the year end.
reserve_committed.source: CFR line B01 Committed revenue balances / not broken out in the AAR

reserve_uncommitted.label: Uncommitted reserve
reserve_uncommitted.plain: Savings the school has not yet earmarked, so it could use them for anything.
reserve_uncommitted.how: The uncommitted revenue balance reported at the year end.
reserve_uncommitted.source: CFR line B02 Uncommitted revenue balances / not broken out in the AAR

reserve_share.label: Reserve as a share of income
reserve_share.plain: How many weeks of running costs the savings would cover: 8% is roughly a month.
reserve_share.how: Revenue reserve divided by total income for the same year, shown as a percentage.
reserve_share.source: Worked out from the reserve and total income lines

in_year_balance.label: In-year balance
in_year_balance.plain: Whether the school spent more or less than it received this year.
in_year_balance.how: Total income less total expenditure for the year. One year below zero is common; it matters when it happens year after year.
in_year_balance.source: Worked out from the total income and total expenditure lines

per_pupil.label: Per pupil
per_pupil.plain: The figure divided by the number of pupils, so schools of different sizes can be compared.
per_pupil.how: Every total divided by the same year's pupil count from the same return, which can differ from the census count.
per_pupil.source: Worked out from the pupil numbers reported alongside each return

real_terms.label: Real terms
real_terms.plain: Figures adjusted for inflation so that different years can be compared fairly.
real_terms.how: Each year's cash figure is scaled to 2025-26 prices using the HM Treasury GDP deflator for that financial or academic year.
real_terms.source: HM Treasury GDP deflators (October 2026), OGL v3

pupils.label: Pupils
pupils.plain: How many pupils the school had in the year, used to work out the per-pupil figures.
pupils.how: The full-time-equivalent pupil number reported with the finance return.
pupils.source: CFR No Pupils / AAR Number of pupils in academy (FTE)

fsm_pct.label: Free school meals
fsm_pct.plain: The share of pupils eligible for free school meals, a common measure of family income.
fsm_pct.how: Percentage of pupils eligible for free school meals as reported with the return.
fsm_pct.source: CFR and AAR % of pupils eligible for FSM

ehcp_pct.label: Pupils with an EHC plan
ehcp_pct.plain: The share of pupils with an Education, Health and Care plan setting out extra support they need.
ehcp_pct.how: Percentage of pupils with an EHC plan as reported with the return (older returns call this a SEN statement).
ehcp_pct.source: CFR and AAR % of pupils with EHCP

dsg_balance.label: Council schools budget balance
dsg_balance.plain: Whether the council's overall schools budget (the Dedicated Schools Grant) is in surplus or deficit.
dsg_balance.how: The council's cumulative DSG balance at the end of the year, in cash terms. Below zero means a deficit, usually driven by special needs costs.
dsg_balance.source: DfE DSG balances published with the Section 251 outturn / pipeline/money/data/la_dsg.json

dsg_per_pupil.label: Council schools budget balance per pupil
dsg_per_pupil.plain: The council's schools budget balance spread across every pupil in its schools.
dsg_per_pupil.how: DSG balance divided by the number of pupils in the council's schools for the same year.
dsg_per_pupil.source: Worked out from the DSG balance and pupil numbers in the finance returns

deficit_total.label: Total deficits
deficit_total.plain: The combined size of the deficits of schools in this area that are below zero.
deficit_total.how: The sum of negative revenue reserves across schools in the area for the year; schools in surplus are not netted off.
deficit_total.source: Worked out from each school's revenue reserve line

in_deficit_pct.label: Share of schools in deficit
in_deficit_pct.plain: The percentage of schools in this area whose savings are below zero.
in_deficit_pct.how: Schools with a negative revenue reserve divided by schools with a full-year return, for the same year.
in_deficit_pct.source: Worked out from each school's revenue reserve line

pta_income.label: PTA income
pta_income.plain: Money raised by the school's registered parents' association in a year, as reported to the Charity Commission.
pta_income.how: Income reported to the Charity Commission by the registered parents' association charities matched to this school, placed in the school year that contains the end of the charity's financial year. Charities with an income of five thousand pounds or less need not register, so many schools with an active association show nothing. Some of this money may reach the school as donations, so it can overlap with the school's donations line and is never added to it.
pta_income.source: Charity Commission register of charities, OGL v3

pta_spending.label: PTA spending
pta_spending.plain: What the school's registered parents' association spent in a year, as reported to the Charity Commission.
pta_spending.how: Expenditure reported to the Charity Commission by the parents' association charities matched to this school, placed in the school year that contains the end of the charity's financial year.
pta_spending.source: Charity Commission register of charities, OGL v3

pta_per_pupil.label: PTA income per pupil
pta_per_pupil.plain: How much the parent-teacher association raised for each pupil in the school.
pta_per_pupil.how: Parents' association income divided by the school's pupils for the same school year; left out when that year's pupil number is not known.
pta_per_pupil.source: Charity Commission register and the school's finance return

trust_central_spend.label: Trust central spending
trust_central_spend.plain: Money the academy trust spends centrally on things shared across its schools, such as finance, HR and IT.
trust_central_spend.how: The trust's central expenditure per pupil as reported in its accounts return; it is paid for partly by keeping back some of each school's funding.
trust_central_spend.source: AAR Trust Total Exp per pupil / not applicable to council-run schools

cfr_line.label: CFR line
cfr_line.plain: One line from the standard return that every council-run school in England files each year.
cfr_line.how: Reported as filed, in cash terms. Income lines start with I, spending with E and balances with B.
cfr_line.source: DfE Consistent Financial Reporting return via the Financial Benchmarking and Insights Tool

aar_line.label: Accounts return line
aar_line.plain: One line from the annual accounts return that every academy in England files each year.
aar_line.how: Reported as filed, in cash terms, for the academic year ending 31 August.
aar_line.source: DfE Academies Accounts Return via the Financial Benchmarking and Insights Tool

status_in_deficit.label: In deficit
status_in_deficit.plain: The school's savings are below zero, so it owes money to its council or trust and will have a recovery plan.
status_in_deficit.how: Revenue reserve below zero in the latest full year.

status_heading_for_deficit.label: Heading for deficit
status_heading_for_deficit.plain: The school still has savings, but has spent more than it received for two or more years running and would use them up within about three years unless something changes.
status_heading_for_deficit.how: Revenue reserve above zero, in-year balance below zero in at least the last two full years running, and at the average rate of those overspends the reserve would run out within three years (exactly three counts).

status_tight.label: Tight
status_tight.plain: The school has very little in reserve, so one unexpected cost could push it into deficit.
status_tight.how: Revenue reserve above zero but under 3% of a year's income.

status_healthy.label: Healthy
status_healthy.plain: The school has a sensible cushion of savings for its size.
status_healthy.how: Revenue reserve between 3% and 8% of a year's income (5% for secondaries), and not overspending year after year.

status_large_reserves.label: Large reserves
status_large_reserves.plain: The school has built up more savings than it needs for a cushion, which may be earmarked for a project.
status_large_reserves.how: Revenue reserve at or above 8% of a year's income (5% for secondaries).

band.label: Intake band
band.plain: Where the school's intake sits nationally on a scale from 1 (least disadvantaged) to 5 (most disadvantaged), used to compare like with like.
band.how: A national quintile of a combined rank of free school meal eligibility and the deprivation of the school's neighbourhood (IDACI).
band.source: DfE finance returns, GIAS and the English Indices of Deprivation 2019, OGL v3

other_dfe_grants.label: Other DfE grants (including pension and NI grants)
other_dfe_grants.plain: Extra grants from the Department for Education on top of the main funding, including the grants that cover rises in teachers' pension and staff National Insurance costs.
other_dfe_grants.how: A container line: the pension and National Insurance grants sit inside it alongside other targeted and one-off grants, and no return separates them out, so this is never a figure for the pension grants alone. Much of it passes straight through to pay and pension costs. For council-run schools it is the additional-grants line I18 up to 2024-25; in 2025-26 that line was removed and these grants moved into I06 other government grants, so 2025-26 is not directly comparable with earlier years. For academies it is other DfE revenue grants.
other_dfe_grants.source: CFR line I18 (to 2024-25) and line I06 (2025-26) / AAR Other DfE revenue grants

gov_funding_pp.label: Government funding per pupil
gov_funding_pp.plain: The government grant money the school received for each of its pupils in the year.
gov_funding_pp.how: Government grants divided by the same year's pupils. For academies, non-government grants and income from other academies are taken out. Council-run schools' grant total includes line I07 other grants and payments, which can hold some non-government money, so the two sectors are not strictly comparable.
gov_funding_pp.source: CFR Grant funding / AAR Total grant funding less non-government and academy income, with the pupil number from the same return

spend_pp.label: Spending per pupil
spend_pp.plain: What the school spent in the year for each of its pupils.
spend_pp.how: Total spending divided by the same year's pupils. The fairest national comparison is the IFS figure for spending by schools themselves in the same phase (primary or secondary), not its all-in figure, which also counts money councils and trusts spend centrally. Academy figures leave out what the trust spends centrally.
spend_pp.source: CFR and AAR Total expenditure, with the pupil number from the same return

gov_vs_spend_gap.label: Funding compared with spending
gov_vs_spend_gap.plain: Government funding per pupil set beside spending per pupil, which shows how much of a school's spending the government grant covers.
gov_vs_spend_gap.how: Both figures for the same year and divided by the same pupils. Spending above government funding is met from money the school raises itself (lettings, catering, donations) or by drawing on its savings; spending below it adds to them. Council-run schools' years run April to March and academies' September to August, and their government grant lines are not strictly comparable.
gov_vs_spend_gap.source: Worked out from the government grant and total expenditure lines of the school's CFR or AAR return

falling_rolls.label: Falling pupil numbers
falling_rolls.plain: The school has fewer pupils than it used to, which brings less funding while many costs stay the same.
falling_rolls.how: Shown when pupil numbers fell by 5% or more across the years on the page, or fell in each of the last three years. This is the site's own rule, not an official measure. Schools are funded mostly per pupil, and costs such as a class teacher do not fall in step, so a well-run school with falling numbers can still find its budget stretched.
falling_rolls.source: Pupil numbers reported with each year's CFR or AAR return

pass_through.label: Income that passed straight through
pass_through.plain: Much of a rise in the school's income was matched by a rise in its staff costs, so it was not extra money to spend.
pass_through.how: Shown for the latest year, from 2023-24 on, when total income rose by 5% or more on the year before and staff costs rose by at least seven-tenths of that rise. This is the site's own rule. Grants for higher teacher pension and National Insurance costs arrive as income and leave as pay, so they add to both sides without adding spending power.
pass_through.source: Worked out from total income and total staff costs in the school's CFR or AAR return

high_send.label: Many pupils with special educational needs
high_send.plain: The school supports more pupils with special educational needs than most schools, which brings extra costs.
high_send.how: Shown when the share of pupils with an Education, Health and Care plan is above the national 5.3% reported by the IFS, or when special needs funding makes up a bigger share of the school's income than at three schools in four. This is the site's own rule. Schools are expected to meet the first part of the extra cost for each pupil from their own budget before council top-up funding starts.
high_send.source: CFR and AAR % of pupils with an EHCP and SEN funding lines; national EHCP share from the IFS

trust_central_spend_pp.label: Trust central spending per pupil
trust_central_spend_pp.plain: What the academy's trust spent centrally for each pupil on shared services such as finance, HR, IT and school improvement.
trust_central_spend_pp.how: The trust's central-services spending divided by all the pupils in its academies, for the same academic year. The academy's own spending per pupil on this site does not include it, so bear it in mind when comparing with council-run schools, whose councils also spend some money centrally. The IFS reports that trusts' central spending per pupil more than doubled between 2016-17 and 2023-24.
trust_central_spend_pp.source: AAR Central Services sheet: Trust Total Exp per pupil, or total expenditure divided by total pupils

pta_gap.label: Parents' association money compared
pta_gap.plain: How much more or less the school's parents' association raised per pupil than those at the schools it is compared with.
pta_gap.how: The school's parents' association income per pupil set against the median for the comparison group, for the same school year. Only registered charities are counted, and charities with an income of five thousand pounds or less need not register, so the gap can reflect registration as much as fundraising. Parents' association money and school donations can overlap and are never added together.
pta_gap.source: Charity Commission register of charities (OGL v3) and the school's finance return

pta_history.label: Parents' association history
pta_history.plain: What the school's registered parents' association raised and spent each year, as reported to the Charity Commission.
pta_history.how: Each annual return is placed in the school year that contains the end of the charity's financial year, using the school's own year (April to March for council-run schools, September to August for academies), and divided by that year's pupils. A charity shared by several schools is split equally between them. A charity with no income reported since 2019 is described as having had a registered PTA until its last year with income. Charities with an income of five thousand pounds or less need not register, so a school with no registered parents' association found may still have an active one.
pta_history.source: Charity Commission register of charities, annual returns, OGL v3

statutory_override.label: The statutory override
statutory_override.plain: A temporary accounting rule that lets councils hold special needs budget deficits apart from their main accounts.
statutory_override.how: Since 2020-21 councils' Dedicated Schools Grant deficits, mostly from special needs spending, have been held in a separate reserve rather than met from their general funds. The override runs to the end of 2027-28, and the IFS quotes an OBR forecast that the total could reach 14 billion pounds by 2028. Under the February 2026 approach, the High Needs Stability Grant pays 90% of each council's eligible deficit at 31 March 2026 from autumn 2026, so balances are expected to fall sharply in 2026-27.
statutory_override.source: DfE section 251 outturn note in pipeline/money/data/la_dsg.json; IFS annual report on education spending 2025-26, p.61

deficit_pp.label: Deficit per pupil
deficit_pp.plain: How far below zero the savings are, spread across the pupils.
deficit_pp.how: A negative revenue reserve divided by the same year's pupils. Most deficits build up over several years in which costs rise faster than funding, and a school in deficit agrees a recovery plan with its council or trust.
deficit_pp.source: Worked out from the revenue reserve and pupil numbers in each school's return

reserve_median_pp.label: Typical reserve per pupil
reserve_median_pp.plain: The savings per pupil of the middle school in the group: half hold more and half hold less.
reserve_median_pp.how: Each school's revenue reserve divided by its pupils for the same year, then the median across the group's schools with a full-year return. Values the source marks as suspect are left out. The median is used so that one very large or very small reserve does not skew it.
reserve_median_pp.source: Worked out from each school's revenue reserve and pupil numbers

schools_in_deficit.label: Schools in deficit
schools_in_deficit.plain: The number of schools in the group whose savings were below zero at the end of the year.
schools_in_deficit.how: Schools with a negative revenue reserve in a full-year return for that year. An academy's figure is its own reserve and does not include money its trust holds centrally. Council-run schools' years run April to March and academies' September to August.
schools_in_deficit.source: Worked out from each school's revenue reserve line in the CFR and AAR

ifs_figure.label: IFS figure
ifs_figure.plain: A figure quoted from the IFS annual report on education spending, in 2025-26 prices.
ifs_figure.how: Quoted exactly as the Institute for Fiscal Studies published it in its annual report on education spending in England 2025-26 (January 2026), in 2025-26 prices using the HM Treasury GDP deflator of November 2025. It is a national figure, not this school's, and the site's own real-terms figures use the newer October 2026 deflator.
ifs_figure.source: Institute for Fiscal Studies, Annual report on education spending in England: 2025-26 (January 2026)
